verses.english: “I shall recite a verse in praise, telling where the earth-devas dwell:
those who cling to the mountain cleft, resolute and composed.
Many, withdrawn like lions, whose hair stands on end in awe,
bright of mind, pure, serene and untroubled.”
Knowing that more than five hundred were in the Kapilavatthu wood,

verses.pali_roman: Tato āmantayi satthā sāvake sāsane rate:
verses.english: the Teacher then addressed the disciples who delight in the teaching:
“The hosts of devas have come. Know them, bhikkhus.”

verses.pali_roman: Te ca ātappa-makaruṃ sutvā buddhassa sāsanaṃ.
verses.english: And they made an ardent effort, having heard the Buddha's instruction.
Knowledge appeared to them, the seeing of non-human beings.
Some saw a hundred, some a thousand, and some seventy thousand.
Some saw a hundred thousand non-human beings,
and some saw them without end: every direction was filled.
Having directly known all of that, having surveyed it, the One with vision

verses.pali_roman: Tato āmantayi satthā sāvake sāsane rate:
verses.english: then addressed, as Teacher, the disciples who delight in the teaching:
“The hosts of devas have come. Know them, bhikkhus —
those whom I shall proclaim to you in words, one after another.

verses.pali_roman: Satta sahassā va yakkhā bhummā kāpilavatthavā,
verses.english: Seven thousand yakkhas, earth-dwellers of Kapilavatthu,
possessed of power, of radiance, of beauty and of renown,
came rejoicing to the wood, to the assembly of bhikkhus.
Six thousand yakkhas from the Himavā, of varied hues,
possessed of power, of radiance, of beauty and of renown,
came rejoicing to the wood, to the assembly of bhikkhus.

vocabulary.meaning: a verse, a stanza — and also fame or repute. The opening line puns on both: the Buddha recites a verse that also praises
a mountain cleft or cave. Where the earth-dwelling devas of the first verse are said to abide
one in whom the hair stands on end — awe rather than fear, said of the assembled beings
non-human being. The general word covering the yakkhas, devas and nagas the list goes on to name
of the Himava, the snowy mountain range. A class of yakkha named by where it dwells

checks.issue: TWO COLUMNS ON EVERY ROW, and the gutter was measured rather than judged: the right column's left edge sits at x 1078-1085 on all twenty-two rows and the longest left-column line stops at x 927. Unlike pages 317 and 318, this sheet has ONE gutter throughout rather than a different one per block.
'Silokamanukassami' is set in BOLD, as the opening words of a spoken unit are elsewhere in this section. The app has no bold layer, so it is recorded rather than reproduced.

The book prints an APOSTROPHE STANDING FOR AN ELIDED VOWEL in ’nanta-maddakkhum, and again at siha’va (44) and vo’ham (57). Kept as the page sets them. They are elision marks, not quotation marks, and a script that normalises quotes would silently change three words.

Verses 59 and 62 are IDENTICAL, and so are 60 and 63 — the list repeats a refrain for each class of being it names. This is the book being what it is, not a duplicate to be collapsed, and check_render walks rather than counts precisely so that repeats like this pass.
